newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion ends up on world trends.
newsitem.headline: India bullion ends up on world trends.

text.p: Gold 24 carat closed 80 rupees higher at 4,470 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,390 rupees as a recovery in the world market triggered fresh speculative as well as physical buying, dealers said.
Limited inflow and hike in the premium of import licences also fuelled buoyancy in the local market after sharp losses witnessed last week.
Meanwhile prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed 1,000 rupees higher at 52,300 rupees per piece after gaining 500 rupees on Thursday.

"Traders witnessed fresh investment buying for gold as some of the operators have booked profit in the booming stock market and this fund is now again flowing into the bullion market," said Babubhai Jain, a leading dealer.
"Meanwhile premium of special import licence for bullion has gone up today to 11.75/12.00 percent from 11.10/11.15 percent on higher buying spree," he said.

A hike in the licence premium and recovery in the world market has pulled up the lending cost of the imported gold which in turn helped local prices bounce back after recent losses. Local gold prices fell to their lowest level in four-and-a-half years last week. Import licence premiums fell to 9.60/9.70 percent.

Silver (.999) closed 105 rupees higher at 6,370 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,265 rupees on the back of a shortage of ready stock while a recovery in the world market prompted speculative buying. Physical buying for silver however remained slow during the day due to a sudden spurt in prices. Silver was up by 115 rupees per kg on Thursday.
Both precious metals have bounced back sharply after recent losses and traders were expecting some resistance from buyers as well as profit-taking in the coming days.
